Overview
Adventure Details
What pulls the crew in: a rumoured prize, a patron with silver, a debt, a curse. Write your own, or roll the Core Rules' Jobs & Quests tables (hook, patron, requirement, time restraint, complication).
Trackers

Clocks, countdowns and timers for the whole adventure. On the GM Screen each one gets a Start button that adds it to the Trackers tool.

GM Notes
Clues & Secrets
Scenes
Hazards & Traps
It's a Trap! (Trapped in the Tropics): roll the d12 trap alone for speed, or across trap, bait, trigger, state and complication (5d12). Adapt what doesn't fit.
Travel

Legs of the journey: where from and to, how far, who leads the way, mishaps and encounters on the road. On the GM Screen a leg's travel time can start as a Ticks tracker.

A ship travels up to its speed in 50-mile hexes a day; sailing northeast, east or southeast in the Dark Caribbean costs 1 hex a day (minimum 1). Roll a maritime event once a leg, or 2-in-6 per hex or per 4-hour watch: the Core Rules' events, encounters and flotsam (d20 / d20 / d12) or Trapped in the Tropics' d12.
Factions

Groups with their own goals. Each faction's clock is a row of boxes: say what fills a box and what happens when the last one fills. On the GM Screen the clock gets a Start button that adds it to the Trackers tool.

Vehicles

The crew's vehicles and the ones they meet. On the GM Screen a vehicle goes to the combat tracker like any foe, its hull as the damage track.

The crew's ship and the ones they meet. Ships come from the Core Rules (raft to ship of the line, forts), Trapped in the Tropics and your homebrew (pb-ship); a template turns one into a ghost ship, a ship of bone, a vessel from the deep or a captain's fleet ship. Every number stays editable. Crew skill modifiers, specialty crew and known shanties are tracked per ship.
Foes, Folk & Bosses
Enemies never roll: a PC attacks (STRENGTH or PRESENCE DR12) and defends (AGILITY DR12) unless the block says otherwise, and takes the enemy's damage minus their armor die. Morale: 2d6 above it breaks them — d6 1-3 flee, 4-6 surrender; "–" never breaks.
Roll a pirate name (d66 ×4: first name, surname, two nicknames) and their Reaction (2d6). It adds an NPC block below — with the numbers of a bestiary NPC if you pick one.
Treasure
Silver, cargo, relics and gear. Cargo values are the adventure's suggestions (d12 per cargo slot). Pick from the Guidebook's gear lists and your homebrew.
